canvas-01.description: Printed sheet 1 carries the street and specials index, a small key map of the township, the colour legend and the Sanborn Map Company title seal on its left side; those parts are outside the mapped area. The map itself fills the right side of the sheet at 50 feet to an inch and is drawn with north toward the bottom of the page. It follows Rahway Avenue, which runs down the sheet from Main Street at the top, past a long run of detached dwellings and small outbuildings, across Woodbridge Creek (crossed by a steel bridge, with the Woodbridge Lumber Co. yard beside it) and on to its junction with Green Street at the lower left. The Woodbridge Pottery Co., with a kiln room and office, and the Monument Theatre (motion pictures) stand near Main Street at the top right. In the middle of the sheet are the Woodbridge Hotel and a brewery near the railroad, and along Green Street a row of small brick-lined stores and shops, a concrete and tile works and a lodge building. The Pennsylvania Railroad passenger station, freight house and several tracks run down the right edge. Berry Street enters from the top left and Nelson Street crosses the lower part. Large areas away from the streets are blank paper. Water pipes (12, 8 and 6 inch) are marked in the streets, and the compass rose stands at the centre right.
notes: Rahway Avenue, Main Street and Green Street are modern names; Green Street meets East Green Street at the Rahway Avenue junction.
Printed names are given as lettered on the sheet, which omit the suffix for Main, Berry, Green and Nelson.
Reading from overview and a few full-resolution crops only; street names lettered along the creek and railroad were not all checked.

Printed sheet 1, 50 ft. Index of streets and specials, key map and legend at the left (cut out of the mask). Map of Rahway Avenue, Green Street, Berry, Main and Nelson with Woodbridge Creek and the railroad, drawn upside down (north toward the bottom). Placed from two hand-picked points (Main/Rahway, Rahway/Green); low confidence.

sheet-2-1.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Woodbridge village at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the top of the page and turned about 15 degrees. Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet from School Street at the left to Fulton Street, and New Street and 2nd Street run parallel to it lower down; William Street bounds the lower left blocks. Along Main Street the north side is a continuous row of two-storey stores and dwellings, with brick buildings near Fulton Street; on the south side stands the First Methodist Episcopal Church, a brick building with a lettered plan, with dwellings and small shops on either side. The blocks between Main and New Streets and between New and 2nd Streets are mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings on deep lots. The upper edge of the part is a heavy line below Fulton and Albert Streets, above which the sheet repeats part of sheet 4, including a fire company building, town hall and jail at the top left. A Sanborn compass rose stands at the right and the railroad runs along the right edge. A large works inset at the lower right (Mutton Hollow Fire Brick Co.) is a separate part, described as part 2.
notes: William Street is North William Street and 2nd Street is Second Street in OpenStreetMap.
Reading made from the overview and a few crops, not from full-resolution crops for every street; the street list may be incomplete.
50 ft. Part 1: Main, Fulton, New, William, 2nd, School, Albert, Pearl (6 detected points). Part 2, inset of the Mutton Hollow Fire Brick Co. at lower right, is not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Mutton Hollow Fire Brick Co., located 1 1/4 miles SW of Fire Co. No. 1 (no street junction; needs location of the works plus parcel corners (locate.py corner) or a modern feature, px_per_ft 7.9 and north_deg from its arrow).

sheet-3-1.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Woodbridge village south and west of School Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The main map runs from James Street in the north, across Main Street and New Street, to 2nd Street at the bottom edge, with Perth Amboy Avenue crossing the west side of the sheet on a slant and meeting Grove Street and New Street near the same point. William Street continues south from School Street on the east edge. The blocks along Main Street are the commercial core of the village: two-storey frame stores and dwellings with several brick buildings on the north side between Perth Amboy Avenue and School Street, among them the Hotel Middlesex near the corner of Perth Amboy Avenue. The Woodbridge Grammar School, a large brick building, stands on School Street at the top right of the sheet, and a Hungarian Reformed Church is drawn north of James Street. South of Main Street the blocks are residential, with frame dwellings and outbuildings on deep lots along New Street and 2nd Street; the area west of Perth Amboy Avenue toward Grove Street and Granville Street is thinly built. A heavy line cuts off the top of the sheet for an inset of Sewaren (described as part 2), which partly overlaps the upper blocks; the area north of James Street shown on the main map is sparsely built. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the main streets, and the lot numbering, block numbers 13, 14, 15, 31, 32 and 48 and the adjoining sheet numbers 2, 4 and 5 appear around the edges.
notes: Perth Amboy Avenue is Amboy Avenue in OpenStreetMap; James Street is North James Street; William Street is North William Street; 2nd Street is Second Street; Granville Street is Grenville Street.
Block numbers printed on the part: 13, 14, 15, 31, 32, 48.

Pilot, 50 ft; fitted 7.90 px/ft. Village centre: James, Main, New, 2nd, Perth Amboy Avenue (Amboy Avenue), School, William, Grove. Part 2, inset of Sewaren (Boynton Lumber Co., Road to Perth Amboy, Old Road, Beach Road, own north arrow), is not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Sewaren, Boynton Lumber Co. (Road to Perth Amboy, Old Road, Beach Road) (no junction identified with a modern street; drawn Road to Perth Amboy not matched; needs step 6b, or anchor on Old Road / Woodbridge Avenue (40.55213,-74.25918) with px_per_ft 7.91 and north_deg about -25 once its pixel is found).

sheet-4-1.description: Sheet 4 covers the district south of the village centre at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 16 degrees. 2nd Street and William Street bound it at the top left, Fulton Street runs down the right side beside the railroad, and Valentine Street crosses the upper blocks on a slant. Below the works are the blocks between 3rd Street and Albert Street, bounded by Smith Street at the left and Augusta Street in the middle, with Perth Amboy Avenue crossing the lower left corner. The buildings are mostly frame dwellings and outbuildings on deep lots, with a few brick buildings and several stores along Fulton Street, one of them lettered as a hotel near the right edge. A heavy line cuts out the large works of M. D. Valentine and Bro. Co., makers of fire brick, with kilns, drying sheds and storage buildings beside the railroad at the left; that inset, drawn at a different rotation, is a separate part not georeferenced here. A fire company building and a small block appear at the top left, and a compass rose stands at the centre right. Berry's Lane runs off Fulton Street on the right. Blocks are numbered 12, 26, 27 and 28, and the adjoining sheets 2, 3 and 7 are lettered on the margins.
notes: Modern names: Augusta Street is Augustus Street, Smith Street is East Smith Street, William Street is North William Street, 2nd Street is Second Street, Perth Amboy Avenue is Amboy Avenue.
Reading made from the overview with few full-resolution crops; street list may be incomplete or not exact (not checked at full resolution).

50 ft. Part 1: 2nd, William, Fulton, Smith, Augusta, Albert, Caroline, Coley, Valentine (12 detected points). The M. D. Valentine & Bro. Co. works inside the heavy outline is drawn at its own rotation and is not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: M. D. Valentine & Bro. Co. works inside the heavy outline, drawn at its own rotation (not examined in time; no street junction inside the outline; needs parcel corners or carried points from part 1 along Fulton Street once its true location is identified).

sheet-5-1.description: This part is the main map of sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 90 degrees on the page so that north lies towards the left. It runs from Barron Avenue at the top to Perth Amboy Avenue at the bottom, bounded on the left by a heavy line and on the right by the sheet edge. Grove, Green, Linden and Myrtle streets cross it, the first two as long slanted streets converging towards the top. The blocks hold the High School, a large pink brick building near the top with the Woodbridge Athletic Association and the First Congregational Church on the block to its left, and frame dwellings with outbuildings on the remaining blocks, numbered 41 to 44b, 54, 57 and 58. School Street and Fulton Street appear at the top right and an unnamed creek runs down the right margin. The sheet carries a compass rose near the right edge. Water pipes of four and six inches are marked in the streets, and a railroad with a coal bin under trestle track is drawn across the very top of the sheet.
notes: Perth Amboy Avenue is Amboy Avenue in OpenStreetMap. Old Grove and Green drawn tilted against modern lines; Grove/Myrtle junction was 9 m off and was dropped.
Placed from four junctions at 3.85 px/ft, 2.6 percent under the 100 ft constant; low confidence.

sheet-5-2.description: This part is the left strip of sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and separated from the main map by a heavy vertical line. Main Street, a 75 foot street, and Grove Street run down the strip as two long parallel streets with lots numbered along their edges, and Metuchen Road joins Main Street from the left near the middle. Dally, Morris and Madison cross between Main and Grove in the lower half of the strip, below Metuchen Road. The blocks, numbered 13, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36 and 37, hold small frame dwellings with outbuildings, St. James Catholic Church and St. James Parochial School No 1 in a large lot to the right of Main Street, and several lots marked vacant. Notes of No Exposure mark the blank area left of the drawn blocks and a vacant fields strip lies between Grove Street and the heavy line. The part has its own north arrow pointing up and to the left, with another on the lower block. Water pipes of four and twelve inches are marked in the streets.
notes: Metuchen Road is Metuchen Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

By position and spacing along Main Street, Dally is today's St James Avenue, Morris is Oak Avenue and Madison is Mattison Street; all three junctions with Main and Grove were detected and agree to about 1 m.
The part continues south of Madison in part 4 of this sheet.

sheet-5-4.description: This part is the boxed block at the bottom centre of sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and set off from the left strip and the main map by heavy lines. It continues the left strip of the sheet southwards: Main Street and Grove Street run down the part as two long parallel streets, Madison crosses them along the top edge, and King George Road leaves Main Street diagonally at the lower left corner. The part has its own north arrow pointing up and to the left, so the streets are drawn turned well away from north, as in the left strip. Block 36 between Main and Grove holds a row of small frame dwellings with sheds and stables along both street fronts, with lot lines running back from each street; a few brick buildings stand near the King George Road corner. A twelve inch water pipe is marked along Main Street and a four inch pipe along Grove Street. The right edge of the part is the heavy line beside block 58 of the main map, and the bottom is the edge of the sheet. The part shows the southern end of the village's Main Street in 1916, where it leaves the built-up area towards Fords and the King George Road, then still lined with scattered houses rather than the continuous frontages of the village centre further north.
notes: Madison is Mattison Street and King George Road is King Georges Road in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from two detected junctions on Madison (Mattison Street) with Main and Grove: low confidence.

sheet-5-5.description: This part is a small boxed inset in the lower half of sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing left, surrounded by heavy lines inside block 58 of the main map. It shows St. James Parochial School No. 2 on the corner of 2nd Street and Perth Amboy Avenue, some distance from the area of the main map: 2nd Street runs up the left edge of the inset and Perth Amboy Avenue crosses its lower part at a slant. The school is a single large frame building marked with its heating (furnace) and lighting (electric), standing in a lot numbered 12C, with a smaller dwelling with outbuildings on the next lot to the right along Perth Amboy Avenue, numbered 184. A hydrant stands at the corner, a four inch water pipe is marked in 2nd Street and a six inch pipe along Perth Amboy Avenue. Below Perth Amboy Avenue the inset shows the edge of the next block, numbered 61, with one small building. The rest of the box is blank paper marked vacant. The inset is the second school of St. James parish; the first, St. James Parochial School No. 1, is drawn beside St. James Catholic Church on Main Street in part 2 of this sheet. Drawing this small separate lot as an inset let the sheet cover it without a sheet of its own, which is common in the smaller Sanborn atlases of this period.
notes: 2nd Street is Second Street and Perth Amboy Avenue is Amboy Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one detected junction (Amboy Avenue / Second Street) with rotation from the drawn street lines and the 100 ft scale: low confidence.

sheet-6-1.description: This part is the main map of sheet 6, the large area right of the heavy vertical line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch (the scale of feet is printed at the lower right), unlike the 100 ft strips on the left of the sheet. It shows the works of the Federal Terra Cotta Co., manufacturers of terra cotta shapes, and of the New Jersey Glue Co., on Cutter Road east of Woodbridge. The terra cotta works fill the upper half: a long range of brick buildings holding pressing shops No. 1 and No. 2, the spraying room, mitre cutting, modelling room, laboratory, chemical storage and plaster storage, with a fitting shed and a block of eight round kilns, each lettered, at the top, and a separate pressing shop No. 3 and laboratory to the right. A mill room, raw stock bins, a machine shop and smaller service buildings stand by the railroad. Cutter Road crosses the sheet from the left on a bridge over a double-track railroad and runs to the right towards the shore of the backwater of Woodbridge Creek. South of the road are the glue works: a concrete warehouse, an evaporating building and smaller buildings. Railroad tracks and sidings curve through the upper left, and salt meadows are marked along the top. Notes on watchman service, power, heat, lights and water supply are printed for both works.
notes: Cutter Road is Cutters Dock Road in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from one hand-picked point, the Cutter Road bridge over the North Jersey Coast Line, with the 50 ft scale and north 21 degrees clockwise of up (from the modern bearings of the railroad, 159.9 degrees, and of Cutters Dock Road at the bridge, which give 20 and 23 degrees); the printed north arrow suggests about 12 degrees. Low confidence.

Parts 2 and 3: left strips at 100 ft (Rahway Avenue, Freeman, Crampton, Grove Avenue; Barron Avenue, Freeman, High), 1 to 2 points each.

sheet-6-2.description: This part is the upper left strip of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and separated from the works map on its right by a heavy vertical line, with a second heavy line below it at the foot of the part. Rahway Avenue runs up the strip as a slightly slanted street labelled with widths of 66 and 90 feet, crossed by Freeman Street at the top and Crampton Avenue about two thirds of the way down, and Grove Avenue meets it near the bottom. At the top the street forks at a small triangular park, where Woodbridge Avenue leaves towards the north east, and the First Presbyterian Church stands on the block above, beside a cemetery block numbered 46. Blocks 45, 14 and 25a and 25b hold small frame dwellings with outbuildings, a club house in block 14 and the Barron Public Library in a large lot on the east side of Rahway Avenue north of Crampton Avenue. Along the left edge the notes No Exposure mark the blank paper beyond the drawn blocks, and a scale note of 100 ft to an inch is printed near the foot. The part has its own north arrow pointing up and to the left. Water pipes of 6 inch and 8 inch size are marked along Rahway Avenue.
notes: Rahway Avenue, Freeman Street, Crampton Avenue are placed from two hand-checked junctions on Rahway Avenue only; low confidence.
Freeman is printed without a suffix and is Freeman Street in OpenStreetMap.
Cemetery and park are drawn at the top of the part; Salt Meadows is lettered on the adjoining works map, not on this part.

Parts 2 and 3: left strips at 100 ft (Rahway Avenue, Freeman, Crampton, Grove Avenue; Barron Avenue, Freeman, High), 1 to 2 points each.

sheet-6-3.description: This part is the lower left strip of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and enclosed by heavy lines on its top and right sides. Barron Avenue runs up the strip as a 66 foot street with a four inch water pipe in it, crossing Freeman Street, which is drawn about three quarters of the way down the part, and High Street is lettered at the foot of the sheet, where the street is cut by the lower edge. Blocks 51, 52, 53 and 54 hold small frame dwellings and outbuildings, mostly one and two storeys, on lots that are numbered along the street edges, and a number of lots at the lower left are marked vacant. A railroad is drawn as a vertical line of dashes along the right side of the strip near the heavy line, labelled as a railroad and with lots beyond it blank. A scale note of 100 ft to an inch is printed at the top of the part. The part has its own north arrow near the bottom, pointing nearly straight up. A fire hydrant and lamp are marked at the Freeman Street corner.

sheet-7-1.description: Sheet 7, part 1 is the main map of Sewaren, on the Staten Island Sound shore east of Woodbridge, drawn at 100 feet to an inch (the sheet is labelled Sewaren P.O., located 1 1/2 miles S.E. of Woodbridge Fire Co. No. 1). It fills the right two thirds of the sheet. Holton Road crosses it east and west near the middle; Broad Street and Cliff Road run north and south through the blocks to the east of it, with Cliff Road following the shore, and Ferry Street closes the lower blocks above a large unsubdivided tract numbered 27. A wedge-shaped block of East Avenue and Sewaren Avenue, with large blocks 18, 24 and 25 laid out as long narrow strips, occupies the centre; the faint outline of a large lettered company name is printed across it. Houses are scattered, mostly two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings on large lots, with a few tile-roofed pink buildings. On the shore are a pavilion and floating dock at the end of Holton Road, boat houses and bath houses along the water, the Sewaren Hotel and Ackers Boat House near Ferry Street, and a long dock. The railroad runs diagonally across the upper left of the part. The top left corner includes blocks 20, 21 and 22 beside Charles Avenue, George Street and West Avenue. The sheet number 7, the Woodbridge, N.J. August 1916 title cartouche, a compass rose and the scale bar are printed here. Separately outlined parts of the sheet lie at left and bottom.
notes: Holton is printed as Holton Road here; OpenStreetMap calls it Holton Street, and the drawn Broad is Broad Street.
Drawn Cliff Road is about 80 m east of Broad Street, but modern Cliff Road is about 156 m east of it, so Cliff Road was left out of the control (shoreline or street change).
Placed from two points only (Broad / Ferry detected, Broad / Holton hand-picked) with the scale and rotation from the config: low confidence.

sheet-7-2.description: Sheet 7, part 2 is the small upper-left corner of the Sewaren sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and separated from the main map at its right by a heavy line that follows West Avenue. The sheet heading printed above it reads Sewaren P.O., located one and a half miles south east of Woodbridge Fire Co. No. 1. A short north arrow, pointing up and to the left, shows that this corner is turned about a quarter turn counter-clockwise from the main map. Sewaren Avenue crosses the part as a wide oblique street running from the upper left down to the right, bordered by narrow lots on its east side. Block 76 lies between Sewaren Avenue and West Avenue and holds a handful of frame dwellings, a shed and a grocery, all drawn in yellow with outbuildings at the rear of long, narrow lots. A water pipe of 6 inch bore runs down the west side of West Avenue and along Woodbridge Avenue. The large area to the left of Sewaren Avenue is lettered as vacant and carries the number 75. Woodbridge Avenue crosses the lower part of the corner from side to side, and below it block 77 is shown mostly empty apart from two pink tile-roofed buildings, a library and an office, at its left, and a heavy railroad line forms the bottom edge of the part, with the legend no exposure printed along it. The part contains no street junction that is drawn in full, only the meeting of Sewaren Avenue with Woodbridge Avenue, so its placement rests on a single point.
notes: Placed from a single hand-picked point (Sewaren Avenue / Woodbridge Avenue) with scale 3.95 px/ft and north -25 degrees taken from the drawn north arrow and Sewaren Avenue's direction: low confidence, rotation uncertain by about 10 degrees.
The part's right edge is West Avenue, whose other side is on part 1, so West Avenue was not used as control.
The modern streets Sewaren Avenue and Woodbridge Avenue keep their printed names.

sheet-7-3.description: Sheet 7, part 3 is the long strip at the left of the Sewaren sheet, between the heavy dividing line on its right and the sheet edge, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It is a separately outlined district with its own north arrow, which points up and slightly to the right. A set of long, narrow north-south blocks, numbered 64, 66, 67 and 70, lies between Strawberry Avenue at the left and Fulton at the right, with Benjamin crossing near the top and Cutter Road closing the strip at the bottom. The blocks are cut into narrow house lots, each holding a two-storey frame dwelling in yellow with outbuildings, with a few pink tile-roofed or brick buildings, among them a tile works at the corner of Strawberry Avenue and Benjamin. Above Benjamin the large blocks are mostly empty, and the left edge carries the lettering of a vacant tract. A six inch water pipe runs along one side of the long block and a dashed line marks it near Cutter Road, where lots are shown with a spring house and a row of dwellings below the road, in block 68. Each street is labelled with a width of 50 feet. An overhead wire marker stands at the corner of Fulton and Cutter Road. The part has no railroad. Its placement rests on two junctions between Strawberry Avenue and the cross streets, so it is a similarity fit and not checked by further control.
notes: Placed from Strawberry Avenue / Benjamin and Strawberry Avenue / Cutter Road, matched to the modern Strawberry Hill Avenue with Benjamin Street and Cutters Dock Road; the fitted scale (4.17 px/ft) is 5 percent above the atlas value and the fitted rotation (28 degrees) is far from the drawn north arrow (about 10 degrees): low confidence.
Modern names: Strawberry Hill Avenue (printed Strawberry Av.), Benjamin Street, Cutters Dock Road (printed Cutter Road); Fulton Street was not found near this part in the modern streets.

sheet-7-4.description: Sheet 7, part 4 is the block at the bottom centre of the Sewaren sheet, outlined by heavy lines and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with its own north arrow pointing straight up. It shows the meeting of Woodbridge Avenue, East Avenue and Cliff Road on the Staten Island Sound shore. Woodbridge Avenue runs from the left across the part, labelled 60 feet wide, and divides the blocks numbered 15 and 16 above from 18 and 19 below. East Avenue comes in from the lower left as a wide street with a six inch water pipe along it, forming a long wedge of block 19 where it joins Woodbridge Avenue. Cliff Road runs down the right side of the part following the shore, with lot numbers lettered along its west side. Block 16 holds St. Johns Chapel, a frame church with a note of heating, stoves and electric lighting, and block 19 holds several dwellings and an automobile garage and shed. Block 17 at the right edge is cut by the shore of Staten Island Sound, where boat houses stand on the water line. A railroad is not shown. An overhead wire marker stands at the junction of Woodbridge Avenue and East Avenue. The upper edge of the part is the heavy line shared with part 1, and the left edge the line shared with part 3 beyond which the lettering reads vacant.
notes: Placed from a single point (East Avenue / Woodbridge Avenue) with scale 3.95 px/ft and rotation from the drawn lines: low confidence.
Cliff Road / Woodbridge Avenue was not used: drawn Cliff Road is displaced against the modern line (see sheet 7 part 1).

sheet-9-1.description: Sheet 9, part 1 is the main map of Port Reading, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and labelled as located 2 miles E. of Woodbridge P.O., with a population of 1000. It covers the upper and left part of the sheet. A regular grid of lettered and numbered blocks (numbers 15 to 33) lies between the Central Railroad of New Jersey main line, which runs north and south along the left edge, and the diagonal line of Woodbridge Avenue, which crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right. Cartaret Avenue, Tappen and Turner Streets run north and south; 1st to 6th Streets run east and west. Building is concentrated in the blocks east of Tappen Street and along Woodbridge Avenue, where a post office, a coal yard, stores and dwellings are drawn, while the blocks west of Tappen Street and along the railroad are largely vacant, divided into numbered lots. A trestle and conveyor runs along the railroad east of Woodbridge Avenue, and a Port Reading Railroad branch crosses the lower left. A water and fire information note, the sheet number 9, the Woodbridge, N.J. August 1916 title cartouche, a compass rose and the scale bar are printed on it. The blocks below the heavy line along Woodbridge Avenue and the boxed area at the right belong to separate parts of the sheet.
notes: In OpenStreetMap the numbered streets are East 2nd Street, East 3rd Street, 4th Street, East 5th Street and West 5th Street, Cartaret is Carteret Street, Tappen is East Tappen Street.

Only four junctions were detected (Turner / 5th, Tappen / 3rd, 4th and 5th); Cartaret Avenue and the 2nd Street junctions were not found. Fitted rotation is about -26 degrees: the modern grid is tilted against the drawn one.
